query: If airlines eliminated the most common cabin-service complaints in the reviews, how much would the average Overall Rating improve?

per_column.name: has_staff_complaint
per_column.rationale: Binary flag for the presence of a staff/cabin-service complaint — a direct operationalization of the intervenable lever the query proposes to eliminate. Not a confounder.

per_column.name: staff_service_rating_low
per_column.rationale: Indicator that staff-service rating is low; another proxy for the poor-service condition to be intervened on. It restates the treatment rather than adjusting for a common cause.

per_column.name: has_service_complaint_text
per_column.rationale: Text-derived complaint flag — again an operationalization of the treatment (cabin-service complaint), not a confounder.

per_column.name: potential_rating_improvement
per_column.rationale: A pre-computed counterfactual delta (the estimated rating change itself). It is the answer/effect estimate, not a variable to adjust for; it embeds a naive uplift with no confounder control.

per_column.name: staff_service_normalized
per_column.rationale: Rescaled staff-service score (0–1). This is the treatment intensity/proxy, not a common cause of both treatment and outcome.

judge.rationale: The added columns correctly identify an intervenable treatment (cabin-service complaints / poor staff service, which an airline could act to remove) and even pre-compute the counterfactual uplift. However, the interventional claim requires adjusting for common causes of both treatment and outcome before the effect can be read off. NOT A SINGLE confounder was added: every column is either a restatement of the treatment or the effect estimate itself. Obvious unnamed confounders available in the source table (Class, Type of Traveller, Route/Airline, Verified) were ignored. The result is a naive difference-in-means, not an identified counterfactual. Fails the what-if test: confounder_quality = 0.0.
